findings.title: `unsubscribe` raises NoMethodError when the user has no `TopicUser` row for the topic
findings.body: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return `nil` (for example, if a user receives an email via mailing-list mode on a new topic before visiting it, or navigates directly to `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` without having previously visited or interacted with the topic). Calling `tu.notification_level` on line 107 will then raise `NoMethodError: undefined method 'notification_level' for nil:NilClass` and return a 500 error. Also, modifying `tu` directly bypasses `TopicUser.change`, which creates the row when absent, sets `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id`, and publishes the change on MessageBus.

findings.title: State-changing `unsubscribe` action runs on GET and acts as a toggle on repeat visits
findings.body: `GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` mutates the user's notification level on a GET request and steps the level down on each request (`watching`/`tracking` -> `regular`, then `regular` -> `muted`). Because email scanners, link previewers, browser prefetching, or a user refreshing the page will issue additional GET requests, a user who was watching/tracking a topic and clicked the link expecting to drop to `regular` will instead be muted on the second GET. Additionally, when the user is navigated to `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` via Ember client-side routing (or when `PostStream.loadTopicView` fetches `/t/:id.json`), the behavior between initial server render (which mutates via `TopicsController#unsubscribe`) and client-side transition (which calls `TopicsController#show` via `loadTopicView`) is inconsistent.
